A virtual image is formed behind the mirror and is located at the position where the extended reflected rays (dashed lines) converge.

Marjorie’s image is as far behind the mirror as she is in front. Note that she and her image have the same color of clothing—evidence that light doesn’t change frequency upon reflection. Interestingly, her left–right axis is no more reversed than her up–down axis. The axis that is reversed, as shown to the right, is front–back. That’s why it seems like her left hand faces the right hand of her image.

(a) The virtual image formed by a convex mirror (a mirror that curves outward) is smaller and closer to the mirror than the object. (b) When the object is close to a concave mirror (a mirror that curves inward like a “cave”), the virtual image is larger and farther away than the object. In either case, the law of reflection applies to each ray.
Diffuse reflection. Although each ray obeys the law of reflection, the many different surface angles that light rays encounter in striking a rough surface cause reflection in many directions.
